_doc: Class-4 (organizing) data. Hand-authored, NOT derived and NOT publisher-declared. Defines the Cybersecurity trunk, the nine limbs, and which limb every published catalog attaches to. See docs/tree-model.md §3 Class 4 and docs/plans/cybersecurity-trunk-and-voice-2026-07-31.md Part A. Every catalog->limb and trunk->limb hop is emitted as an `organizes` edge (relationship_class `organizing`, publication_status `editorial`) and must be badged 'Control Atlas structure' in the UI, never as a source name.

_syntheticCatalogsDoc: These three catalog_ids carry real limb content but ship with no catalog root node of their own (their records land orphaned). The build (Part A.3) synthesizes a `<catalog_id>:CATALOG` node for each so they attach to their limb exactly like the 16 real roots; their same-catalog children then attach via the existing structural rule. Baseline catalogs (nist-800-53b, fedramp-rev5) are deliberately excluded — baselines are Class-2 applicability overlays, never tree spine (docs/tree-model.md §3.2).
_residualLimbsDoc: Total-trunk-connectivity backfill (owner 2026-07-31: 'everything must connect to the trunk, period'). Catalog_ids here have neither a real nor a synthetic catalog root — they are baseline / applicability sets. Their orphan nodes connect to the trunk via an editorial `organizes` edge to the named limb, satisfying connectivity while keeping baselines OFF the structural spine (they remain Class-2 applicability overlays). Any orphan whose catalog_id HAS a real catalog root is instead backfilled structurally to that root by the build (same-catalog rule); the build fails loudly if ANY node still cannot reach the trunk.
